title: Which of these six squares end in the digit six?
description: The video decides which squares end in six by looking only at the last digit of each number. Keeko doubts the answer after thinking only the numbers ending in six give squares ending in six.
teaching_notes: One idea: the last digit of a square depends only on the last digit of the number. Numbers ending in four and in six both give squares ending in six. Watch for students who forget the numbers ending in four.

video_script.why: The child sees that the units digit of a square is fixed by the units digit of the number, so a quick test is possible without working out the whole square.
video_script.substitution: Square only the last digit of each number and read the last digit of that result.
video_script.anchor: the six numbers thirty eight, thirty four, forty six, fifty six, seventy four and eighty two in a row
video_script.wrong_answer: only the numbers ending in six
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko picks only forty six and fifty six, because they end in six. Numbers ending in four also give a square ending in six, since four times four is sixteen.
video_script.payoff_line: The squares of thirty four, forty six, fifty six and seventy four end in six

final_answer.value: 34², 46², 56² and 74² end in 6; 38² and 82² end in 4
final_answer.spoken: the squares of thirty four, forty six, fifty six and seventy four end in six

never_show: the exercise numbers with 4 in the units place
maths_rules: the units digit of a square depends only on the units digit of the number
38 ends in 8, 8 × 8 = 64, so 38² ends in 4; 82 ends in 2, 2 × 2 = 4, so 82² ends in 4
34 and 74 end in 4, 4 × 4 = 16, so 34² and 74² end in 6
46 and 56 end in 6, 6 × 6 = 36, so 46² and 56² end in 6
the slip: only 46² and 56² is wrong, because 34² and 74² also end in 6
video_script.design: One idea: only the last digit matters. Wrong idea: only numbers ending in six give squares ending in six. The six numbers stay in the anchor band.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; six numbers in the anchor band, 38, 34, 46, 56, 74 and 82, each with a small square sign and an empty digit box

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.nums: the six numbers appear in a row, each with a small square sign
marks.ask: an empty digit box appears after each number

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>Square each of these numbers, thirty eight, thirty four, forty six, fifty six, seventy four and eighty two.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which of the six squares end in the digit six?

beats.on_screen: the question holds still and the six digit boxes glow

marks.stop: the six empty boxes glow in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 23 × 23 = 529 written in long multiplication; the last digit 9 is joined to 3 × 3 only

marks.last: the last digit 9 lights up and joins to 3 × 3

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Twenty three times twenty three is five hundred twenty nine.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Its last digit, nine, comes from three times three alone.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The other digits never reach the units place, so only the last digit of the number matters.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers thirty eight, thirty four, forty six, fifty six, seventy four and eighty two are squared.

beats.on_screen: To find: which squares end in 6

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which of these squares end in six.

beats.on_screen: 38 ends in 8: 8 × 8 = 64, ends in 4. 82 ends in 2: 2 × 2 = 4, ends in 4.

marks.eight: 38 shrinks to its last digit 8, and 8 × 8 = 64 is written
marks.two: 82 shrinks to its last digit 2, and 2 × 2 = 4 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='eight'/>Step one, use only the last digit. Thirty eight ends in eight, and eight times eight is sixty four.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Eighty two ends in two, and two times two is four. Both squares end in four.

marks.four: 34 and 74 shrink to their last digit 4, and 4 × 4 = 16 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step two, thirty four and seventy four end in four.
Four times four is sixteen, which ends in six.

marks.six: 46 and 56 shrink to their last digit 6, and 6 × 6 = 36 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='six'/>Step three, forty six and fifty six end in six.
Six times six is thirty six, which ends in six.

marks.check: 74 × 74 = 5476 is written and its last digit is ringed

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check one of them. Seventy four times seventy four is five thousand four hundred seventy six, which ends in six.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 34², 46², 56² and 74² end in 6; 38² and 82² end in 4
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The squares of thirty four, forty six, fifty six and seventy four end in six.
The squares of thirty eight and eighty two end in four.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: only 46 and 56 give squares ending in 6; 34 and 74 are added back

marks.fix: 34 and 74 are ticked in the bubble too

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks only the numbers ending in six give squares ending in six.
<bookmark mark='four'/>But four times four is sixteen, and sixteen ends in six too.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Numbers ending in four belong on the list as well.
